title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer thresholds and regional failover backoff
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: We observed a production incident where transient latency spikes in a single region caused the SLO enforcer to prematurely trigger aggressive load-shedding and cascade into regional failover. This hotfix tightens thresholds, adds hysteresis and per-region backoff smoothing, and improves observability so the enforcer is resilient to short-lived spikes without sacrificing SLO guarantees. Summary of changes: 1) Implemented a hysteresis module for SLO state transitions to require sustained violations before shedding traffic. 2) Added per-region exponential backoff with cap and jitter to prevent synchronized failover. 3) Persisted per-region backoff state in Redis to survive restarts. 4) Exposed new metrics (slo_enforcer.region_backoff_active, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_window_ms, slo_enforcer.shed_decisions) and updated dashboards/alerts. 5) Tightened default thresholds for tail-latency detection and added a config flag slo_enforcer.enable_regional_hysteresis (off by default for older clusters). Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests added; load test harness validated behavior with synthetic spikes. Canary rollout plan described in the runbook; observed no negative user impact in 24-hour canary. CI initially failed on lint due to naming, then passed after small rename. This is a targeted hotfix; change is backward compatible and gated behind a feature flag. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests (local canary) - [x] Metrics/dashboards updated - [x] Runbook updated - [x] Feature flag added - [x] Canary verified - [x] Merge via squash
